# Context Window Management Strategies

Dimension 2 of the LLM Token Budgeting research. Covers truncation,
summarization, RAG, sliding windows, compression, and caching strategies for
production systems. Source details in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Strategy Comparison

| Strategy | Token Reduction | Accuracy Impact | Latency | Best For |
|----------|----------------|-----------------|---------|----------|
| Truncation | High | Information loss | None | Cost-constrained, short memory OK |
| Summarization | Moderate (varies) | Risk of trajectory elongation [56] | LLM call overhead | Medium conversations |
| RAG | High (few K tokens) | Depends on retrieval quality | ~1s end-to-end [10] | Large knowledge bases |
| Long Context | None | Degrades with length [6][7] | 30-60s at full window [10] | Small-medium documents |
| Compression (ACON) | 26-54% peak tokens [3] | 95% retained via distillation [3] | Compression overhead | Long-horizon agents |
| Prompt Caching | N/A (same tokens) | None | 85% reduction [17] | Repetitive prefixes |
| Memory Pointers | Up to 99.99% [5] | None (full data preserved) | Reduced [5] | Large tool outputs |

## Truncation

Naive truncation drops oldest messages, creating jarring context loss. Prioritized
truncation distinguishes must-have content (current message, system prompts) from
optional (conversation history) [21].

The Deep Agents SDK truncates tool inputs at 85% of context window capacity,
replacing full content with disk pointers [21].

## Summarization

ConversationSummaryBufferMemory keeps recent N tokens verbatim while summarizing
older content via LLM. Configurable via `max_token_limit` parameter [58].

**Warning**: Summarization can cause "trajectory elongation" — smoothing over
failure severity causes agents to miss that they are stuck in loops [56]. This
makes observation masking (which preserves failure visibility while removing
token-heavy output) preferable in agent contexts [56].

## RAG vs Long Context

LC generally outperforms RAG in QA benchmarks, especially Wikipedia-based
questions [10]. RAG excels at fragmented information and dialogue-based
contexts [10]. Speed difference: RAG averages ~1 second end-to-end vs 30-60
seconds for long context [10].

Summarization-based retrieval performs comparably to LC; chunk-based retrieval
significantly underperforms both [10].

## Context Compression

ACON framework [3]:
- 26-54% reduction in peak token usage on AppWorld, OfficeBench, Multi-objective QA
- Gradient-free optimization — works with API-accessible models (no fine-tuning)
- Distilled compressors retain 95% accuracy
- Enables smaller LMs to improve by 32% (AppWorld), 20% (OfficeBench), 46%
  (Multi-objective QA)

## Memory Pointer Pattern

Stores large tool outputs externally, passes short references to LLM context [5]:
- Molecular Grid Retrieval: ~1,234 tokens vs ~20.8M estimated conventional
- Safety Data Sheet: 842 vs 6,411 tokens (~7× reduction)
- Framework-agnostic, no architectural changes to LLMs or tools
- Three components: input inspector, original tool, post-processor

## Programmatic Tool Calling (Anthropic)

Claude writes Python code orchestrating multiple tools in sandboxed execution.
Only final output returns to context [22]:
- 37% token reduction on complex research tasks (43,588 → 27,297 tokens)
- Budget compliance workflow: 200KB raw data → 1KB results
- Best for 3+ dependent tool calls, parallel operations, large datasets

## Prompt Caching

Anthropic prompt caching pricing [17]:

| Operation | Cost Relative to Base |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Cache read | 0.1× (90% savings) |
| 5-min cache write | 1.25× |
| 1-hour cache write | 2.0× |

Minimum cacheable tokens: 4,096 (Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5), 2,048 (Sonnet 4.6),
1,024 (Sonnet 4.5/4.1/4). Up to 4 breakpoints per request. Multi-turn
conversation: ~80% savings after first turn [17].

Broader ecosystem: implicit caching (automatic, free) vs explicit (higher
upfront, saves on reads). Batch processing: 50%+ discount. Combined
strategies achieve 70-90% total cost reduction [55]. Monthly spend example:
$720 → $72 after enabling caching [50].

## Cognitive Degradation Resilience

The CSA CDR framework (November 2025) provides health probes, starvation
monitors, token pressure guards, fallback logic, and lifecycle monitoring [29].
65% of enterprise AI failures in 2025 were attributed to context drift or memory
loss, not raw context exhaustion [29].

## Decision Framework

1. **Static prefixes** (system prompts, tool definitions) → prompt caching
2. **Large tool outputs** → memory pointers or PTC
3. **Long conversation history** → summarization with observation masking
4. **External knowledge** → RAG for large corpora, LC for small documents
5. **Agent tasks** → ACON compression for long-horizon execution

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published decision heuristics for dynamically switching between RAG and
  long context in hybrid systems
- Limited quantitative data on combining multiple strategies simultaneously
- Production metrics for "cognitive degradation" detection are not standardized
- Testing strategies for validating that truncation/summarization preserves
  critical information are not well documented
